mainTopic: Which services need the right hand when only כהונה is written, and what job רבא's 'יד יד' derivation has for each opinion
overview: The גמרא keeps testing the rule that a service needs the right hand when the פסוק mentions a כהן. First it challenges רבי שמעון from זריקה: only כהונה is written there, yet a left-handed זריקה is פסול. אביי answers that רבי שמעון does argue on this, in a ברייתא. Then the גמרא challenges the other side: if כהונה alone teaches 'right hand,' why does רבא need his 'יד יד' comparison for קמיצה? The answer is that כהונה covers the קמיצה and 'יד יד' covers קידוש הקומץ. The גמרא then asks what 'יד יד' is for according to רבי שמעון. He either does not require קידוש הקומץ or allows it with the left hand. He also already learns the right hand for the קמיצה itself from 'כחטאת וכאשם'. The answer is that 'יד יד' teaches that even the קומץ of a מנחת חוטא must be taken with the right hand. Finally the גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה, about a pebble or grain of salt that came up in the handful.

steps.title: Challenge from sprinkling the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: זריקה mentions only כהונה, yet a left-handed זריקה is פסול, and רבי שמעון does not seem to argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at sprinkling the blood. The פסוק only mentions the כהן there. Yet we learned in a משנה that sprinkling with the left hand is disqualified, and רבי שמעון does not argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that, for רבי שמעון, a mention of כהונה alone is not enough to require the right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that the right hand is required only when the פסוק mentions both a finger and כהונה. For זריקה only כהונה is written, yet the משנה says left-handed זריקה is פסול with no argument recorded. This suggests that even רבי שמעון agrees כהונה alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling or throwing the blood of a קרבן onto the מזבח
Priesthood; the פסוק saying the act is done by 'the כהן'
The left hand
Disqualified; the service does not count

phrases.english: But there is sprinkling of the blood
concerning which only the priesthood is written,
phrases.notes: The פסוק for sprinkling mentions the כהן, but it says nothing about a finger.

phrases.english: and we learned: if he sprinkled with the left hand, it is disqualified,
and Rabbi Shimon does not disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי זְרִיקָה דְּלָא כְּתִיב בַּיהּ אֶלָּא כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבי שמעון's rule that the right hand is required only where both a finger and כהונה are written.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's position that כהונה alone does not require the right hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules left-handed זריקה פסול although only כהונה is written, and records no argument from רבי שמעון.

steps.title: אביי: רבי שמעון disagrees in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי שמעון does argue on left-handed זריקה. His disagreement appears in a ברייתא, even though the משנה does not record it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי שמעון does disagree, in a ברייתא. It was taught: if he collected the blood with his left hand, it is disqualified, and רבי שמעון says it is fit. If he sprinkled with his left hand, it is disqualified, and רבי שמעון says it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי שמעון by bringing a ברייתא where רבי שמעון explicitly allows left-handed קבלה and left-handed זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence of the משנה does not mean רבי שמעון agrees. The ברייתא shows he holds a left-handed זריקה is כשר, because only כהונה is written there. His rule stays consistent: without a finger mentioned in the פסוק, the right hand is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
He collected the blood in a vessel (קבלה)
Deems it fit or valid

phrases.english: Abaye said: He disagrees in a baraita,
as it is taught: if he collected the blood with the left hand, it is disqualified,
and Rabbi Shimon deems it fit;
if he sprinkled with the left hand, it is disqualified,
and Rabbi Shimon deems it fit.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an outside source showing the assumed agreement does not exist
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the משנה records no argument, רבי שמעון must agree that left-handed זריקה is פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון explicitly disagrees in a ברייתא and allows left-handed קבלה and זריקה.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, כהונה alone does not require the right hand. That is why he allows left-handed קבלה and זריקה.

steps.title: Why does רבא need 'hand, hand' for the handful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now challenges the other side. If כהונה alone teaches 'right hand,' why does רבא need a 'יד יד' comparison to teach that קמיצה is done with the right hand?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about רבא's teaching that we compare the word 'hand' to the word 'hand' for removing the handful? Why do I need it? We already learn it from the mention of the כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the view that a mention of כהונה alone is enough to require the right hand, and asks why רבא then needs an extra source for קמיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of קמיצה says 'וקמץ הכהן,' so it mentions כהונה. If כהונה alone means the right hand, קמיצה should already require the right hand. רבא's 'יד יד' derivation then looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Hand, hand'; רבא's comparison between the same word in two passages (a גזירה שוה)
Removing a handful from a מנחה
It is derived, it comes out from

phrases.english: But that which Rava said:
"hand" "hand" for removing the handful,
phrases.notes: רבא links the word 'hand' in the passage about the מצורע to 'hand' by קמיצה, so קמיצה must also be done with the right hand.

phrases.english: why do I need it?
It can be derived from the priesthood!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:12, 'and the כהן shall remove his handful.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge, now against the view that כהונה alone requires the right hand.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a mention of כהונה alone requires the right hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If כהונה alone teaches right hand, רבא's 'יד יד' derivation for קמיצה would be pointless, because the קמיצה פסוק already mentions the כהן.
steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not against רבי שמעון. It is aimed at the view that כהונה alone is enough, because only under that view does רבא's source look extra.

steps.title: One for the handful, one for sanctifying it
steps.stepSummary: The answer: both sources are needed. One teaches the right hand for the קמיצה itself, and the other teaches it for קידוש הקומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: One source is for removing the handful, and one is for sanctifying the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבא's 'יד יד' is not extra after all, because there are two separate acts that need the right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהונה teaches that the קמיצה itself must be done with the right hand. רבא's 'יד יד' adds a second act, קידוש הקומץ, which is placing the handful into a כלי שרת. That act must also be done with the right hand, so each source has its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from the מנחה
Sanctifying the handful by placing it into a second כלי שרת

phrases.english: One is for the handful,
and one is for the sanctification of the handful.
phrases.notes: This means putting the handful into a second holy vessel, which also has to be done with the right hand.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each source a separate application
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both כהונה and 'יד יד' teach the same thing, so one of them is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: כהונה covers the קמיצה, and 'יד יד' covers קידוש הקומץ.

steps.title: For רבי שמעון, why is רבא's source needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the answer works for רבי שמעון. He either does not require קידוש הקומץ at all, or allows it with the left hand, so רבא's 'יד יד' cannot be for קידוש הקומץ under his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי שמעון, who does not require sanctifying the handful, and also according to the one who says רבי שמעון does require it but accepts it with the left hand, why do I need רבא's 'hand, hand'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty against the previous answer, this time from רבי שמעון's position. Step 6 continues this challenge, and step 8 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 4 gave רבא's 'יד יד' the job of teaching the right hand for קידוש הקומץ. For רבי שמעון that job does not exist, because he either does not require קידוש הקומץ or allows it with the left hand. So the גמרא asks what רבא's 'יד יד' is for under his view. The next step rules out the קמיצה itself as its job.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not require
According to the one who says
He fully deems it valid

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּלָא בָּעֵי קִידּוּשׁ קוֹמֶץ,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, who does not require sanctification of the handful,
and also according to the one who says
that Rabbi Shimon requires sanctification of the handful,
but deems it fit with the left hand –
phrases.notes: These are two different reports of רבי שמעון's view. Under either one, a right hand is not needed for sanctifying the handful.

phrases.english: why do I need Rava's "hand" "hand"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּלָא בָּעֵי קִידּוּשׁ קוֹמֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4 using רבי שמעון's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבא's 'יד יד' derivation according to רבי שמעון, given step 4's answer that it teaches the right hand for קידוש הקומץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי שמעון, קידוש הקומץ either is not required or is valid with the left hand. So רבא's 'יד יד' cannot be teaching the right hand for it, and its purpose under his view is unclear.
steps.whyThisMatters: Each side must account for every source. A derivation that has no job under one opinion forces the גמרא to look for its real purpose.

steps.title: The right hand for the קמיצה itself is already known from another source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues the challenge. According to רבי שמעון, the 'right hand' rule for the קמיצה itself is already learned from רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא's פסוק, so the extra 'יד' still has no job.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the extra 'יד' teaches the right hand for the קמיצה itself, that won't work for רבי שמעון. He already learns that from רבי יהודה son of רבי חייא. רבי יהודה said: What is רבי שמעון's reason? The פסוק says: 'It is most holy, like the חטאת and like the אשם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes off the last possible job for the extra 'יד' according to רבי שמעון. The 'right hand for the קמיצה itself' rule already comes from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the גמרא showed that, for רבי שמעון, רבא's 'יד יד' can't be about קידוש הקומץ. Now it adds that it can't be about the קמיצה itself either. רבי שמעון learns that from the comparison of the מנחה to a חטאת and an אשם, so רבא's 'יד יד' looks completely unused.

keyTerms.meaning: The act of taking the handful itself (as opposed to putting it into a vessel afterward)
Most holy: the highest level of sacrifice
Like the sin offering and like the guilt offering

phrases.english: And if it is for the taking of the handful itself,
according to Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא נָפְקָא,
phrases.english: that is already derived from Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Chiyya,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Chiyya said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: This means his reason for not requiring the handful to be put into a כלי שרת.

phrases.english: Because the verse says:
"It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לִקְמִיצָה גּוּפַהּ, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge of step 5 by removing the last possible use of the second 'יד' for רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 4, as it applies to רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי שמעון, the right hand for the קמיצה itself already comes from 'כחטאת וכאשם', so the extra 'יד' is left with no job.

steps.title: How the חטאת and אשם comparison works
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains the פסוק. If the מנחה is done by hand, it follows the חטאת and needs the right hand. If it is done with a vessel, it follows the אשם and the left hand is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he comes to do it by hand, he does it with the right hand, like a חטאת. If he comes to do it with a vessel, he may do it with the left hand, like an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא explains how the פסוק's comparison to חטאת and אשם gives a rule about which hand to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחה is compared to two offerings. A hand-done service follows the חטאת, which needs the right hand. A vessel-done service follows the אשם, where the left hand is allowed. The קמיצה is always done by hand, so for רבי שמעון it already needs the right hand from this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: By hand, directly with the hand
With a vessel
The right hand

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the left hand is ever allowed for the קמיצה itself. The 'left hand like an אשם' part applies only when the service is done with a vessel. Taking the handful is always done by hand.

phrases.english: If he comes to perform it by hand,
he performs it with the right hand, like a sin offering;
if he comes to perform it with a vessel,
he may perform it with the left hand, like a guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא לְעוֹבְדָהּ בַּיָּד – עוֹבְדָהּ בְּיָמִין, כְּחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 6, showing why it already covers the right hand for the קמיצה.
steps.raayaObject: That for רבי שמעון the קמיצה itself already needs the right hand without the extra 'יד'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'קדש קדשים היא כחטאת וכאשם', as explained by רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא

steps.title: The extra source is needed for the sinner's מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the extra 'יד' teaches that even the קומץ of a מנחת חוטא must be taken with the right hand. Otherwise we might have thought a 'plain' offering could be taken with the left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for the handful of a sinner's מנחה. You might have thought: since רבי שמעון said a sinner's offering should not be fancy, even taking its handful with the left hand should be valid. So the extra 'יד' teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a job for the extra 'יד' according to רבי שמעון. It teaches the right-hand rule for the מנחת חוטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a sinner's offering is deliberately kept plain so that it is not 'fancy'. That idea might have led us to allow a lesser, left-handed קמיצה there. The extra 'יד' blocks that thought: even the מנחת חוטא needs the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for… (introduces the special case where a source has a job)
The meal offering brought by a sinner
You might have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
Fancy, of high quality
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the extra 'יד' is not wasted. It teaches that even a sinner's plain מנחה needs a right-handed קמיצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the challenge that started in step 5. רבא's 'יד יד' now has a job even according to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: It is needed only
for the handful of a sinner's meal offering.
It would enter your mind to say:
since Rabbi Shimon said
that his offering should not be fancy,
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's reason why a sinner's מנחה gets no oil or frankincense.

phrases.english: then when he takes its handful with the left hand too,
it should be valid.
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְקוֹמֶץ דְּמִנְחַת חוֹטֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 5–7 by finding a special case where the extra 'יד' is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a unique case for the extra source (לא נצרכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a sinner's offering is meant to be plain, a left-handed קמיצה might be valid for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra 'יד' teaches that even the מנחת חוטא's קמיצה must be done with the right hand.

steps.title: New משנה quote: a pebble or salt grain in the handful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting the משנה's case: a כהן took the handful and a pebble or a grain of salt came up in his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took the handful, and a pebble or a grain of salt came up in his hand…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next discussion by quoting a new line of the משנה. The discussion of this case comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right-hand discussion is finished. Now the גמרא turns to a new problem: something that isn't flour got mixed into the handful. That could make the קומץ less than a proper full measure.

keyTerms.meaning: He took the handful (of flour from the מנחה)
A small stone or pebble
A grain of salt

phrases.english: If he took the handful, and a pebble came up in his hand,
or a grain of salt,

steps.triggerLanguage: קָמַץ וְעָלָה בְּיָדוֹ צְרוֹר, אוֹ גַרְגֵּר מֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the right-hand discussion and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the case of a pebble or grain of salt that came up in the handful. The ruling and discussion follow.
